theory.intro: Large areas of land are measured in hectares (ha) and square kilometres (km$^2$) rather than square metres.
facts: $1\text{ ha} = 10\,000\text{ m}^2$ (a square $100$ m by $100$ m).
Record hectares with **ha** and square kilometres with **km$^2$**. Both are units of area.
Use **ha** for paddocks, parks and sports grounds; use **km$^2$** for suburbs, forests and countries.
steps: Choose hectares for a block of land or square kilometres for a large region.
For hectare equivalents, use $10\,000\text{ m}^2=1\text{ ha}$. Count how many hectares the square metres make, or how many square metres the hectares make.
Record the area with its unit: ha, m$^2$ or km$^2$.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Choose the more suitable unit, hectares or square kilometres, for a farm paddock.
(b) Choose the more suitable unit for a large forest.
(c) A forest covers $13$ square kilometres. Write its area using the unit symbol.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Hectares suit a block of land such as a paddock.
(b) Square kilometres suit a large region such as a forest.
(c) $13\text{ km}^2$

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Record $73\,000\text{ m}^2$ in hectares.
(b) Record $5.7$ ha in square metres.
Order these land areas from smallest to largest: $38$ ha, $410\,000\text{ m}^2$ and $46$ ha.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Record all three areas in hectares.
$410\,000\div10\,000=41\text{ ha}$
$38\text{ ha}<41\text{ ha}<46\text{ ha}$
From smallest to largest: $38$ ha, $410\,000\text{ m}^2$, $46$ ha.

workedExamples.question_text: Two neighbouring paddocks have areas of $260\,000\text{ m}^2$ and $19$ ha. Find their total area in hectares.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Record both areas in hectares before adding.
$260\,000\div10\,000=26\text{ ha}$
$26+19=45\text{ ha}$

foundation.question_text: Choose the more suitable unit for the area of a community garden: hectares or square kilometres.
foundation.solution_text:
A community garden is land-sized rather than region-sized.
Hectares are more suitable.

foundation.question_text: Choose the more suitable unit for the area of a large national park: hectares or square kilometres.
foundation.solution_text:
A large national park covers a region-sized area.
Square kilometres are more suitable.

foundation.question_text: A national park covers five square kilometres. Record its area using the unit symbol.
foundation.solution_text:
The symbol for square kilometres is km$^2$.
$5\text{ km}^2$

development.question_text: A reserve covers $750$ hectares. Record its area using the unit symbol.
development.solution_text:
The symbol for hectares is ha.
$750\text{ ha}$

development.question_text: A large forest covers $2.4$ square kilometres. Explain why square kilometres are a suitable unit for its area.
development.solution_text: A large forest covers a large region, so square kilometres are suitable for recording its area.

development.question_text:
A wetland covers $45\,000\text{ m}^{2}$.
Record its area in hectares.
Which is larger: $80$ ha or $900\,000\text{ m}^{2}$?
development.solution_text:
Each $10\,000\text{ m}^2$ is $1$ ha.
$900\,000\text{ m}^2=90\text{ ha}$
$90\text{ ha}>80\text{ ha}$
$900\,000\text{ m}^2$ is larger.

development.question_text: A woodland covers $1.6$ square kilometres. Record its area using the unit symbol.

A land record states an area of $320\,000\text{ m}^{2}$.
Write this area in hectares.

mastery.question_text:
Three reserves cover $85$ ha, $700\,000\text{ m}^{2}$ and $900\,000\text{ m}^{2}$.
Order them from smallest to largest.
mastery.solution_text:
$700\,000\text{ m}^2=70\text{ ha}$
$900\,000\text{ m}^2=90\text{ ha}$
$70\text{ ha}<85\text{ ha}<90\text{ ha}$
From smallest to largest: $700\,000\text{ m}^2$, $85$ ha, $900\,000\text{ m}^2$.

mastery.question_text:
A conservation area contains two parcels of $1\,250\,000\text{ m}^{2}$ and $65$ ha.
Find the total area in hectares.

A report describes a small school oval as covering $12\text{ km}^{2}$.
Explain why the unit is unreasonable and give a more suitable large-area unit.
mastery.solution_text:
Square kilometres describe a large region, so $12\text{ km}^2$ is unreasonable for a small school oval.
Hectares are the more suitable large-area unit.
